patterns.usage_note: Casual spoken contraction of としても (〜たって is the colloquial counterpart of 〜ても); here it grants a claim already on the table and the second clause brushes it aside as making no difference. The 仮定 sibling supposes a scenario that has not come about (明日から始めるとしたって), while にしたって leans on nouns naming a real person or case (部長にしたって). Polite としましても is the same expression at higher register; としたところで is close but adds ところで's sense that the supposition would change nothing.

examples.ruby: いくら安[やす]いとしたって、三[みっ]つも買[か]うのは多[おお]すぎる。
examples.english: Even granting they're cheap, buying three of them is too many.

examples.ruby: 先輩[せんぱい]の言[い]い分[ぶん]が正[ただ]しいとしたって、今[いま]さら計画[けいかく]は変[か]えられない。
examples.english: Even granting my senior's version of it is right, the plan can't be changed at this point.

examples.ruby: その噂[うわさ]が事実[じじつ]だとしたって、私[わたし]は驚[おどろ]かない。
examples.english: Even assuming that rumor is true, it wouldn't surprise me.

glosses: even X (an actual case in point)
patterns.usage_note: Casual spoken contraction of にしても attached to something real and already established — a person, an organization, a place — and granted as an extreme or representative case (部長にしたって "even the boss, for his part"); the following clause is usually negative or deflating. Where the 仮定 sibling supposes a case that has not come about (手伝うにしたって), this one starts from a fact. Polite にしましても is the same expression at higher register; にしたところで adds the sense that it would make no difference.

examples.ruby: 部長[ぶちょう]にしたって、この状況[じょうきょう]は予想外[よそうがい]だっただろう。
examples.english: Even the boss can't have seen this situation coming.

examples.ruby: この駅[えき]にしたって、昔[むかし]は畑[はたけ]しかなかったそうだ。
examples.english: Even this station — there was nothing but fields here once, they say.

examples.ruby: 一度[いちど]や二度[にど]失敗[しっぱい]したにしたって、諦[あきら]める必要[ひつよう]はないよ。
examples.english: So you slip up once or twice — that's no reason to give up.

glosses: no matter how much … , it's no use
patterns.usage_note: Attaches to the ta-form (だとこで・だところで after the voiced sound changes of 五段 ガ・ナ・バ・マ行 verbs): the speaker frames the action as futile, so the second clause carries a negative or a judgment like 無駄だ・意味がない rather than reporting a past fact. This entry typically names an effort actually being made or pressed for at the moment of speaking, where the 仮定 sibling entertains it as a bare supposition. Unlike ものの, which concedes something that actually happened, たところで supposes an action that would change nothing, and it is cooler and more dismissive than ても. とこで is a very casual clip of ところで; the same clip also serves the unrelated temporal ところで ("just as …"), so the futility reading depends on a negative or dismissive second clause.

examples.ruby: 今[いま]から急[いそ]いだとこで、終電[しゅうでん]には間[ま]に合[あ]わないよ。
examples.english: Hurrying now isn't going to get us on the last train.

examples.ruby: どれだけ悩[なや]んだとこで、答[こた]えなんて出[で]てこないよ。
examples.english: No matter how long you agonize over it, no answer is going to come.

examples.ruby: 必死[ひっし]に頼[たの]んだとこで、あの人[ひと]の気[き]は変[か]わらないよ。
examples.english: You can beg all you like; that one isn't going to change her mind.

patterns.usage_note: Concessive にしろ used of something already established: you grant what actually happened and insist the main point stands regardless. It is commonly doubled as 〜にしろ〜にしろ to list alternatives, and it contrasts with the 仮定 sibling, which concedes a supposition not yet the case (値上げするにしろ). On the formality scale it sits between the stiffer, more written にせよ and the softer conversational にしても. Note that な-adjectives and nouns also take である before it in careful writing, and that the form is identical to the imperative of にする, so context decides.

examples.ruby: 本人[ほんにん]が忙[いそが]しかったにしろ、返事[へんじ]くらいはできたはずだ。
examples.english: Granted he was busy, he could at least have answered.

examples.ruby: 短[みじか]い付[つ]き合[あ]いにしろ、隣[となり]の店主[てんしゅ]の人柄[ひとがら]はよく分[わ]かった。
examples.english: Short as our acquaintance was, I got a clear sense of what the shopkeeper next door was like.

examples.ruby: 以前[いぜん]断[ことわ]られたにしろ、頼[たの]み直[なお]す価値[かち]はあると思[おも]う。
examples.english: Granted they turned us down before, I still think it's worth asking again.
